slides.title: Gemini 4 Model Lineup Google’s Gemini 4 Model
slides.text: Gemini 4 Model Lineup Google’s Gemini 4 Model Lineup Gemini 4 Neon -  Default for most coding & debugging $3 / $15 - in/out Gemini 4 Carbon - for harder reasoning and long-running coding tasks. $2 / $10 in November, then $4 / $20 Gemini 4 Hydrogen - Fast, low-cost for simple fixes, unit tests, and codebase questions - $1.5 / $7.5 Gemini 4 Argon - skip it for new workflows - use Neon instead https://deepmind.google/models/gemini/ https://9to5google.com/2026/11/18/gemini-4-neon-announcement/ Gemini Models and Agent Harnesses We suspect that Gemini models could use agentic harness under the hood. A Gemini endpoint could serve a single model or orchestrate multiple calls, models, tools, and verification. Its interface alone cannot reveal the implementation. Harnesses can improve performance substantially, but can add cost & latency Google reports Neon scoring 12.8% with mini-SWE versus 39.0% with Antigravity https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-neon/ Google’s recent research explores improving AI agents by modifying their harnesses - prompts, tools, memory, and orchestration - while keeping model weights frozen. Harness² improved LAB partial-pass rates by up to 11.8 % while keeping model weights frozen - https://github.com/google-research/harness2 Recent Google research papers: Harness²: Recursive Agent Harnessing for an Open World https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14224 Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18856 +

slides.title: AGI is Here ? AGI is Here ?
slides.text: AGI is Here ? AGI is Here ? https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=us_pnC6ETNA Alan Turing, the British mathematician and computer-science pioneer. He proposed the Turing test in 1950 , in his paper “Computing Machinery and Intelligence.” He called it the “imitation game.” ARC-AGI = Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus for AGI - a family of tests - by François Chollet ARC-AGI-1 (2019) - colored input/output grids, infers the transformation rule, and produces the output for a new input ARC-AGI-2 (2025) - similar grids, more complex combinations of rules, multi-step reasoning, and symbolic interpretation. ARC-AGI-3 (2026) - interacts with unfamiliar, turn-based, game-like environments without explicit instructions. Must explore, discover the rules and goals, and plan actions efficiently. Humanity’s Last Exam - 2,500 expert-level questions across many subjects GAIA tests real-world research and tool use SWE-bench evaluates fixes to actual software repositories WebArena and OSWorld test actions in websites and computer applications METR evaluates autonomous task completion. Together, these approaches reveal capabilities that any single score can miss No single accepted test certifies AGI; modern benchmarks measure reasoning, practical work, tool use, and autonomy rather than human-like conversation alone. https://arcprize.org Alan Turing François Chollet

slides.title: CALM = Common Architecture Language Model CALM =
slides.text: CALM = Common Architecture Language Model CALM = Common Architecture Language Model CALM AI assistant can read your code (Javascript, Python, ...) and draft the CALM JSON file following JSON Schema. CALM tools can validate the file in CI and generate a diagram or documentation from the same description. Validation step is checking the model against rules; it does not, by itself, verify what’s actually deployed. CALM turns static architecture diagrams into version-controlled JSON models that teams can use to generate diagrams and automatically check designs against approved patterns Morgan Stanley’s team, including engineer Matthew Bain , started the working group in August 2023, and open-sourced version 1.0 through FINOS in August 2025 Use CALM when diagrams go stale or security reviews repeat the same checks. Model services, databases, data flows, and controls, then validate designs before deployment Morgan Stanley reported using CALM for more than 1,400 internal deployments. Vexa uses it in continuous integration to check that its meeting platform follows an approved design https://www.linkedin.com/in/matthewbain/ https://github.com/finos/architecture-as-code https://www.bankingdive.com/news/morgan-stanley-open-source-software-development-finos-calm/758406/ https://docs.vexa.ai/architecture/architecture-as-code

slides.title: AI News Replit: 32 Opus agents beat one
slides.text: AI News Replit: 32 Opus agents beat one agent 18.9x to 3.7x Agents modified NumPy's source code - optimized selected internal code paths exercised by the benchmark Replit supplied the library’s source code and workloads; the agents modified the code in 2 hours; Then replit rebuilt and tested the modified library A single Claude Opus agent reached only 3.7x speedup, while a swarm of 32 agents reached an 18.9x speedup (x5 times more) Gains depended on separable tasks and a shared coordination board The strongest solo model did worse as teams grew https://frontier.replit.com/throwing-headcount-at-the-problem/ You don't need long context https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.05306 NVIDIA researchers demonstrated that AI agents retained nearly unchanged task accuracy even when their context was reset after every action Across tested long-input and long-running tasks, accuracy suffered little or no degradation. This is challenging the assumption that complex work requires enormous context windows Conclusion - frequently compact history into short handoff notes, preserving essential state rather than entire transcripts. Potentially more efficient agents Results do not establish that long context is universally unnecessary

slides.title: Meta e-means Speeds Up Clustering Meta e-means Speeds
slides.text: Meta e-means Speeds Up Clustering Meta e-means Speeds Up Clustering 10–45x faster GPU clustering, beating classic k-means https://arxiv.org/html/2611.09501 Tricks: exponential moving averages, automatic parameter selection, and crowded-cluster splitting to revive unused centroids At scale, it grouped 10 Bln embeddings into 16 Mln clusters in 2.5 passes, outperforming classic 25-pass result Available through Faiss (Facebook AI Similarity Search) library, it can accelerate vector-index construction, quantization, and data curation https://e-means.github.io Reminder about classic k-means: Choose the number of clusters k and pick k initial centroids randomly Assign every data point to its nearest centroid based on distance Recalculate each cluster's centroid by taking the mean of all data points currently assigned to it. Repeat Choosing Optimal k Elbow Method: Plot WCSS (inertia) against a range of k values; look for the "elbow" point where adding more clusters yields diminishing returns. Silhouette Analysis: Measure how similar a point is to its own cluster compared to other clusters (higher average silhouette score is better).
